gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the plug-in Schumacher '100A/200A engine start' is a wall-powered assist with limits: the car must have a battery in it, the unit charges for a required 2 minutes before it will crank, it stops each crank after 7 seconds and then makes you wait 3 minutes. No result says either that this number is an engine-start (cranking) rating, while the '1,200 A' on Battery Tender's charger plus jump-pack units is a peak rating from a lithium pack that needs no outlet. The two amp figures measure different things and can't be compared.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited and the top results. Schumacher's category page (cited) returned HTTP 429, so I could not read it. Advance Auto's SC1309 page (cited) showed only a 'We're offline for a tune-up' notice. ChatGPT's own answer only says the Schumacher units 'require an electrical outlet'. Clamp & Crank lists SC1281 100 A next to NOCO GB40 1,000 A peak and DEWALT 1,600 peak amps. It says the Schumacher 'must stay plugged in' but gives no crank time, cool-down or pre-charge wait, and doesn't explain that the two kinds of amp rating differ. BatteryTrail gives Battery Tender's '3 to 5 seconds' crank advice. It lists Craftsman as '100 cranking A' and packs as '5000A peak' but never compares the two, and says nothing about cool-down, pre-charge or the need for a battery in the car. None of these pages has the 2 min / 7 s / 180 s cycle or the 5 s / 30 s pack cycle side by side.
decides: It answers the question ChatGPT left the shopper with. Schumacher's 100–200 A 'engine start' only helps at home, plugged into 120 V, with a weak battery still in the car. It is a garage assist, not a jump starter, and its amp figure can't be set against pack peak amps. A shopper who wants one device that charges at home and also jumps the car on the road should get a Battery Tender Charge N Start. The 1120 is $149.95 and in stock; the 4120 is $179.95 and out of stock. The trade-off is slower charging: 1 A or 4 A, against Schumacher's 6 A with 30–40 A boost. A shopper who only needs garage charging plus an occasional start keeps ChatGPT's Schumacher pick.

findings.label: Engine-start cycle: pre-charge wait / max crank / cool-down
findings.value: 2 min charging before it will crank; up to 7 s per crank; then a required 180 s cool-down
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1281 Owner's Manual, page 9 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual says: 'Wait for ready' charges for 2 minutes; 'Crank the engine until it starts or 7 seconds pass'; after repeated cranking during a 3-minute ready period, it enters a 'mandatory 3 minute (180 second) cool down state'. If it is extremely cold or the battery is under 2 V, charge for 5 minutes first. This is the SC1281 (100 A / 30 A boost / 6 A), which matches ChatGPT's $79 card. A search snippet from a different scan of the manual said 3 s, so crank time may vary between manual revisions.

findings.label: Engine start needs mains power and a battery in the car
findings.value: Live grounded 120 V AC outlet required; manual warns that engine start without a battery in the vehicle 'could cause damage to the vehicle's electrical system'
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1281 Owner's Manual, page 9 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Both requirements are stated in the manual's Engine Start procedure.

findings.label: Engine-start cycle: pre-charge wait / max crank / cool-down
findings.value: 2 min charging before it will crank; up to 7 s per crank; then a required 180 s cool-down
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1309 Owner's Manual, page 10 of 30 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The 200 A wheeled unit has the same cycle as the 100 A SC1281. The display counts down from 180 to 0. The procedure says to plug into a grounded 120 V outlet and warns against use without a battery in the car. If the engine doesn't start, charge 5 more minutes before cranking again. Engine-start mode exits automatically after 2 h.

findings.label: What Engine Start is for
findings.value: 'Provides additional amps for cranking an engine with a weak or run-down battery. Always use in combination with a battery.'
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1309 Owner's Manual, page 8 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual itself frames the 200 A as help for the car's battery, not a replacement for it.

findings.label: Schumacher uses two different amp units
findings.value: Plug-in SC1667: '250 cranking amp (12V) engine start'; lithium pack SL1672: '1000 peak amp engine start'
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric Manual 10A Car Battery Charger and 250A Engine Starter, SC1667 (Schumacher Electric store)
findings.note: I read the store's product text with storecheck.py search. The SL1672 wording comes from https://www.schumacherelectric.com/products/4-in-1-lithium-jump-starter-and-portable-power-pack-1000-peak-amp-12v-with-wireless-charging, read the same day. The same maker rates plug-in chargers in cranking amps and lithium packs in peak amps, so a 100 A charger next to a 1,000 A pack is not a 10x difference on the same scale. This is the footnote for the table.

findings.label: Jump rating / charge rate / price
findings.value: 1,200 A peak from an internal lithium pack; 1 A ISM charger/maintainer; $149.95, in stock
findings.source_title: Charge N Start 1120 — 1 Amp Battery Charger & 1200 Amp Jump Starter (Battery Tender)
findings.note: I read this with storecheck.py search on batterytender.com, where it shows as available. The maker's text says '1200 peak Amps', gas engines up to 6.0 L, diesel up to 4.0 L, 'Crank for up to 5 seconds'. Plugged into the wall it maintains the car battery; unplugged, the pack jump-starts with no outlet.

findings.label: Jump rating / crank cycle / charge rate / price
findings.value: 1,200 A peak; crank up to 5 s with 30 s between attempts; 4 A charger; $179.95, out of stock
findings.source_title: Charge N Start 4120 — 4 Amp Battery Charger & 1200 Amp Jump Starter (Battery Tender)
findings.note: I read this with storecheck.py search; available=false. The maker's text says 'Crank for up to 5 seconds per attempt with 30 seconds between attempts'. The 1100 page (1,000 A peak, 1 A, $139.95, in stock) gives the same 5 s / 30 s rule. Compared with Schumacher: no 2-minute pre-charge, 30 s rest instead of 180 s, no outlet needed. But it charges at 4 A, against the Schumacher's 6 A with 30–40 A boost.
